_about: Public-domain Jean-Pierre Camus (1584-1652), bishop of Belley and disciple of Francis de Sales, for the Word Hoard: the seventeenth-century English translations of his devotional and moral works: A Discours between an Hermite called Nicephorus (1630), A Spirituall Combat and A Draught of Eternitie (Douai), The Spirituall Director Disinteressed (Rouen, 1633), Admirable Events translated by S. Du Verger (1639) and The Loving Enemy (1667), from Internet Archive scans. The Spirit of St Francis de Sales stays on the Francis de Sales shelf. Added 2026-10-18 by lane A, round 37 (my pick); Adam may veto the whole shelf. Every printing dated before 1930, so public domain in the US. No uids minted.

camus-discours-hermite-1630: A Discours hapned betwene an Hermite called Nicephorus and a yong Lady called Mistresse Petronilla, tr. P. S. P. (printed with permission, 1630)
camus-spirituall-combat: A Spirituall Combat: a tryall of a faithfull soule, tr. M. C. P. of the English College of Douai (Douai: the widow of Mark Wyon; catalogued 1632)
camus-draught-eternitie: A Draught of Eternitie, tr. Miles Carre, priest of the English College of Douai (Douai: the widow of Marke Wyon; catalogued 1632)
camus-spirituall-director-1633: The Spirituall Director Disinteressed, according to the spirit of B. Francis of Sales (Rouen, M.DC.XXXIII)
camus-admirable-events-1639: Admirable Events: selected out of foure bookes, tr. S. Du Verger (London: Thomas Harper for William Brooks, 1639)
camus-loving-enemy-1667: The Loving Enemy, a famous true history, tr. Major Wright (catalogued 1667)

_alternates.camus-copies: Admirable Events (1639, the Abel Roper issue, and admirableeuentss00camu); Diotrephe (1641), Nature's Paradox (1652), Elise (1655), A True Tragical History (1677) and Forced Marriage (1678): title pages unreadable

_excluded.camus-other: The Spirit of St Francis de Sales (PG 9184, all copies) and The Beauties of St Francis de Sales (1829), selections from the same work; they belong with the Francis de Sales shelf
